title: Dog-Trade Defenses Need Proof, Quarantine, and Abolition by 2030
excerpt: Stolen-pet claims, transport cruelty, and disease risks demand police records, quarantine, and public accountability—not tradition claims without proof.
body_html:
Family dogs reportedly targeted by theft networks face a brutal fate: confinement in wire cages and long-distance transport without confirmed food, water, or veterinary oversight. Those allegations demand police records, court documents, and inspection findings—not invented scenes or slogans. Without verifiable incident records, no honest campaign can name victims, locations, convictions, or supply-chain links.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

“Farm-raised dogs” is a claim requiring evidence: licensed premises, ownership records, animal-health certificates, transport permits, quarantine compliance, and a traceable chain from origin to sale. A label cannot prove lawful sourcing. Nor can an allegation prove that every animal in trade was stolen. Authorities must publish seizure records, prosecutions, inspection results, and origin data so families and communities can judge the system.

Rabies risk demands urgent protection

Rabies exposure occurs when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. WHO guidance makes clear that care must begin before symptoms develop. Household exposures and commercial transport are separate dimensions of biosecurity failure; one must not be falsely presented as proof of the other.

Vietnamese communities deserve visible enforcement

Families protecting companion animals, public-health workers, investigators, and local leaders need transparent enforcement against poisoning, theft, illegal transport, and quarantine evasion where documented. Lawful activity, regulatory breaches, and criminal conduct require clear separation. SDE's demand goes further than any single enforcement action: nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
